newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait MPs want slowdown in improving Arab ties.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait MPs want slowdown in improving Arab ties.

text.p: Ten leading Kuwaiti MPs on Saturday presented the parliament with a proposal to slow the government's normalisation of ties with Arab states seen as Iraq sympathisers during the 1990-91 occupation of Kuwait.
The proposal, presented mainly by Islamist MPs, was referred to a parliamentary committee reviewing the government's programme.

Following Saturday's parliamentary session, acting Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Sabah al-Ahamad al-Sabah told reporters that Kuwait had not severed ties with countries in question -- mainly Sudan, Yemen and Jordan -- in order to seek their resumption.
In recent days Kuwait has taken measures which appeared to be the start of improving ties with the three countries.
Jordan and Kuwait this week resumed direct air links for the first time since the 1990 invasion of the tiny Gulf Arab state while a Sudanese minister made the first visit to Kuwait since the crisis.
Yemen's President Ali Abdullah Saleh met in Sanaa this week with a team of Kuwaiti intellectuals including two former ministers.
